gen-gf-unkempt-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoined: Expressive is the first word that comes to mind for Unkempt, whose letters look built from rods rather than carved blades. Noto Sans NKo Unjoined is the quieter one, a plain sans with wide openings on its small letters.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-noto-sans-old-south-ar: Noto Sans Old South Arabian reads clean and approachable, its curved strokes stopping short before they turn inward. Unkempt is the one to make noise, with a single flat line weight through every glyph, and the body font simply keeps going.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-ojuju: A steady line with no pressure variation gives Unkempt its blunt, commanding look. Ojuju follows with a slight swell on the bowls and wide s curves that barely curl in, like lightly flexed spring wire.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-overpass: Unkempt has a crossbar on its t as hefty as the stem, which gives every word a commanding stamp. Overpass, a modern sans-serif, answers by keeping its strokes uniform within a word and its e shapes unmistakably open.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-palanquin: Palanquin brings curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths, a contemporary sans that stays easy on the eye beside the heavy heading. Unkempt's stroke weight never wavers, and that is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-philosopher: Loud meets tidy here, with Unkempt's expressive letters leaving no hairlines to squint at, even when they shrink down. Unkempt does the shouting best, while Philosopher, a clean sans, softly thins its arches where they leave the stem.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-pontano-sans: Pontano Sans reads contemporary and light, its c terminals opening wide while the strokes stay low in contrast. Unkempt brings strokes as constant as bent wire, and that blunt consistency is the strongest thing the pair has.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-pt-sans: PT Sans reads approachable, with c forms that sweep open like arcs and a low-contrast sans build. And Unkempt, drawn like toothpaste squeezed in one steady line, gives the pair its strongest quality: a loud heading over a friendly body.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-quattrocento-sans: Commanding and expressive up top, Unkempt gives its crossbars the same fatness as the stems they connect, and its gaps keep c from becoming o. Quattrocento Sans then settles into a low-contrast plain sans that feels clean and smooth over a long read.
